2110: Handling loads by hand looks free, but the cost shows up in payroll, sick leave, overtime and the idle truck. See how to calculate this figure with numbers.
2111: Handling loads by hand looks free because the cost does not show up on any line of the spreadsheet. There is no invoice called "manual handling". It shows up diluted: in payroll, in sick leave
2112: I thought this might interest you:
2116: This article shows how to calculate that cost with numbers you already have at hand, and then compare it with the investment in equipment.
2118: Start with the simplest: how many people are on handling, how many hours a day and what the real hourly cost of that labor is. Real hourly cost includes payroll charges, not just the salary. Multiply by the days worked in the year and you already have the number nobody usually looks at.
2119: That is why the first result is a shock: a small team, in a routine of a few hours a day, adds up to an annual figure that is often greater than the very equipment that would solve the problem.
2120: The costs that do not go into the calculation and should
2122: Manual handling does not scale. When volume doubles, the only way out is more people or more overtime, and both cost more per unit moved. A machine absorbs the peak without renegotiating anything.
2124: Carrying weight repeatedly causes injury, medical certificates and sick leave. Besides the direct cost, there is the cost of replacing the person in the middle of the shift and the labor liability, which nobody wants on the balance sheet.
2126: Torn bags, crushed boxes, bruised fruit. Every damaged item is product you bought or produced and will not sell. In bag and fresh produce operations, that loss alone already pays for part of the equipment.
2128: Slow unloading means freight standing in the yard. Depending on the contract, that becomes demurrage or lost priority on the next load. And even when it does not become an invoice, it becomes a delay on your own line.
2130: Heavy work has the highest turnover in the factory. Every replacement means selection, hiring, training and low productivity in the first weeks.
2132: Mechanized handling swaps variable cost for investment. Once installed, the conveyor or elevator consumes energy and maintenance, and delivers the same flow every day, regardless of who is absent. The people who were carrying move to checking, packing and quality roles, which add more value.
2133: It is not about reducing the team: at most of the customers we serve, the team stays the same and the operation starts handling a volume that used to be impossible without hiring.
2134: How to assess the payback honestly
2135: Use the real hourly cost, with payroll charges, not the nominal salary.
2136: Consider the volume peak, because that is where the manual operation breaks down.
2137: Add damage and truck waiting time, even with a conservative estimate.
